method: Public-repository static audit and deep control-flow tracing; issue tracker excluded as evidence.

findings.finding: The release workflow falls back to the Android debug key when production signing secrets are absent, but still proceeds to publish the APKs. The filename gains a debug-signed suffix; publication itself is not blocked.
findings.impact: A publicly installed debug-signed build cannot be upgraded in-place by a later production-signed build. This can strand users on an incompatible signing lineage and destroys confidence in release provenance.
findings.fix: Fail the release job unless every signing secret is present. After signing, run apksigner verify --print-certs, reject the Android Debug certificate, compare the SHA-256 certificate digest with a pinned release fingerprint, and publish only after that gate. Keep debug-signed artifacts in a separate non-release workflow.

findings.finding: Offline playback launches a local Playable without a port of Apple's PlaybackMeta/media identity. The code explicitly states that progress may be attributed to whatever engine item the session currently points at.
findings.impact: Watching a downloaded movie or episode can update progress, watched state, scrobbling, or auto-next context for the wrong title—especially after another streamed item was active earlier in the session.
findings.fix: Create a platform-neutral PlaybackContext carrying contentId, videoId, media type, season/episode, profile owner, title and poster. Build it from DownloadRecord and require PlayerScreen/session creation to receive it before local playback starts. Add a regression test that plays downloaded B after streamed A and proves only B changes.

findings.confidence: High-confidence risk; runtime behavior should be integration-tested
findings.finding: Downloads enable automatic redirects while applying arbitrary source request headers, but there is no explicit cross-host redirect policy that strips credentials or origin-bound headers.
findings.impact: Referer, Authorization, cookies, proxy headers, or add-on tokens may follow a redirect to a different host depending on HttpURLConnection behavior and header type.
findings.fix: Handle redirects manually. Resolve each Location, enforce HTTPS/host policy, and drop Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization plus add-on-sensitive headers on origin change unless an explicit trusted redirect policy permits them.

findings.finding: The libmpv wrapper forwards only the raw MPV_EVENT_END_FILE event id. MpvPlayer cannot read mpv_event_end_file.reason, so it classifies every end event after playback has once started as natural EOF.
findings.impact: A decoder error, network failure, reconnect exhaustion, stop, or other non-EOF terminal event after the first frame can be reported as hasEnded=true. The host may mark the title watched and auto-advance instead of showing an error or retrying.
findings.fix: Fork or extend the JNI seam to expose END_FILE reason and error. Set hasEnded only for MPV_END_FILE_REASON_EOF; map ERROR to hasError with the native error code; ignore or separately handle STOP/QUIT/REDIRECT. Add tests for EOF, manual stop, midstream network failure, decode failure, and source replacement.

findings.finding: onPlayerError sets hasError=true, but load does not reset hasError for the next item.
findings.impact: After one failed stream, a later healthy stream can inherit a permanent error state and keep the error UI/retry logic active.
findings.fix: Reset all per-item terminal state at the start of load, ideally by constructing a fresh PlayerState. Ensure onPlayerError clears hasEnded and buffering. Add error-then-success and source-switch tests.

findings.finding: startNextQueued marks the head record downloading and calls startTask. If storageShortfall fails, startTask marks that record failed and returns without continuing to the next queued item.
findings.impact: A single queued item that fails disk preflight can leave free slots unused and stall later valid downloads until another unrelated lifecycle event drains the queue.
findings.fix: Make startTask return a StartDisposition. On preflight/URL rejection, keep draining in a bounded loop. Prefer one fillAvailableSlots owner rather than recursive start-next calls. Add a queue test: head fails preflight, second item must start immediately.

findings.finding: The -3000 self-heal path calls clearTask, which immediately starts the next queued download, then directly restarts the failed record with startTask.
findings.impact: The retry can exceed maxConcurrentDownloads by one and violates the queue ordering/concurrency contract precisely during an error path.
findings.fix: Do not directly restart after clearTask. Requeue the retry at the head with a retry marker, then let fillAvailableSlots be the only starter. Add an invariant assertion and a test that active byte tasks never exceed the configured cap during self-heal.

findings.finding: main has no enforced required status checks.
findings.impact: A broken build, failed security analysis, or untested release change can land on main without any repository-level gate.
findings.fix: Require platform build, unit test, lint/static analysis, secrets scan, and release-artifact verification checks. Require them on pull requests and block force-push/bypass except a tightly controlled emergency role.

findings.finding: The custom CodeQL workflow excludes Swift and Kotlin, while the Java/Kotlin autobuild for the audited commit failed because NDK 27.0.12077973 was not installed.
findings.impact: Neither mobile codebase has dependable CodeQL coverage, despite workflow presence suggesting otherwise.
findings.fix: Use manual CodeQL build mode. Install the exact JDK/SDK/NDK, run the real Gradle compile tasks, add Swift analysis where supported, and make missing-language analysis a failing required check rather than a tolerated gap.

findings.finding: Semgrep is run with failure suppression, and a missing SARIF file is replaced with an empty SARIF result.
findings.impact: Scanner failure can be reported as a successful empty scan. A green workflow does not prove analysis ran.
findings.fix: Remove failure suppression, validate that SARIF contains a Semgrep invocation/result set, upload it only after a successful scan, and make scanner startup/configuration failures fatal.

findings.finding: The Android workflow assembles APKs but does not execute the substantial JVM test corpus, the instrumentation suite, or a lint task. lint is configured as fatal in Gradle, but assemble is not lint.
findings.impact: Many repository tests and lint rules provide no merge protection. Player, profile, download, sync and catalog regressions can compile and ship.
findings.fix: Add lintFullDebug, lintPlayDebug, testFullDebugUnitTest, testPlayDebugUnitTest and connected/device tests. Publish reports and make all required. Add release-variant tests where release-only behavior exists.

findings.finding: app/Tests contains a large contract/security test corpus, but project.yml defines no Xcode test target or test scheme. The standalone harness compiles only a small hand-selected subset and is not wired into the release workflow.
findings.impact: Most Apple tests are non-executable in the generated Xcode project and do not protect releases.
findings.fix: Add VortXTests targets for each applicable platform in XcodeGen, attach app sources through testable modules, create schemes, and run xcodebuild test in a secretless PR workflow. Retain standalone harnesses only for intentionally dependency-free contracts.

findings.finding: The updater trusts an install URL from the appcast and opens it directly. There is no host allow-list or artifact digest verification in the client.
findings.impact: A compromised or incorrectly signed feed path can direct users to an unexpected APK location. Stable signing mitigates installation of a different signer, but the release workflow currently also permits debug signing.
findings.fix: Allow-list HTTPS release hosts, reject redirects outside the allow-list, include SHA-256 and size in the signed feed, verify the downloaded artifact before launching installation, and pin the expected signing certificate after download.

findings.finding: Download index persistence failures are swallowed. In-memory records are updated even when atomic write/rename/fallback persistence fails.
findings.impact: The UI can report a durable state that disappears after restart. Completed downloads may become orphan files, and queued/paused records can vanish without an actionable error.
findings.fix: Return or publish persistence failures, preserve the last-good index, write a checksum/versioned backup, and retry on a serialized store actor. Do not acknowledge terminal completion until the record is durably committed.

findings.finding: Initialization failures for multiple subsystems are caught and can silently disable profiles, sync, media, downloads or updates.
findings.impact: A partially initialized app can look healthy while important functionality is absent.
findings.fix: Record structured startup health, expose degraded-mode diagnostics, retry recoverable components, and fail closed when identity/security-critical initialization fails.

findings.finding: The Android download API has the same stale-return behavior when an existing paused record is resumed.
findings.impact: Immediate UI and coordinator decisions can use the wrong state.
findings.fix: Return DownloadStore.record(id) after resume/requeue, or expose an async/state-flow API rather than returning snapshots.

findings.finding: Offline HLS asset downloading is not implemented on Android.
findings.impact: Segmented streams that are downloadable on iPhone/iPad cannot be downloaded on Android.
findings.fix: Use Media3 DownloadService/DownloadManager with HLS stream keys, persistent requirements, DRM policy and local playback integration.

findings.finding: The season/batch download coordinator available on iOS is absent on Android.
findings.impact: Android users must resolve and queue episodes one at a time; source continuity and quality policy are not shared.
findings.fix: Port the platform-neutral batch plan and source-ranking inputs, then use Android's queue as the executor. Keep profile/title identity explicit.

findings.finding: The auto-delete-watched preference is persisted but the deletion behavior is not wired.
findings.impact: The settings UI promises storage reclamation that never occurs.
findings.fix: Observe the profile-scoped finished-watched signal, guard against active playback/live tasks, and delete only completed local records. Add profile-switch and currently-playing tests.

findings.finding: Raw torrent-to-download conversion remains unwired.
findings.impact: Some torrent sources can play through the streaming server but cannot be converted into durable offline files.
findings.fix: Define one supported path—debrid resolve to stable HTTP, or a foreground local-server transfer with resumability—and reject unsupported torrent downloads before creating a misleading record.

findings.finding: Failure to promote the worker to foreground execution is ignored while the large download continues.
findings.impact: The OS can stop the work under background limits while the UI still expects durable transfer behavior.
findings.fix: Treat foreground promotion as a required precondition for large/long transfers, or explicitly downgrade to a constrained/retry state with a user-visible reason.

findings.finding: setMuted is not idempotent. Repeating setMuted(true) can overwrite the saved pre-mute volume with zero.
findings.impact: Unmuting can restore silence rather than the user's prior volume.
findings.fix: Store previous volume only on the false-to-true transition; restore only on true-to-false. Track mute state explicitly and test repeated mute/unmute calls.

findings.finding: The PlayerState contract says hasError and hasEnded are mutually exclusive, but ExoPlayer's error path can set hasError without clearing hasEnded.
findings.impact: The UI can simultaneously treat playback as ended and failed, producing incorrect auto-next/retry behavior.
findings.fix: Centralize terminal transitions in a reducer and assert exclusivity. Every error transition must clear ended; every EOF transition must clear error.

findings.finding: External subtitle mounting depends on a recognizable URL extension. Extensionless or signed URLs can be silently skipped.
findings.impact: Valid add-on/community subtitles fail on common CDN URLs whose type is carried by content-type or query parameters.
findings.fix: Use declared subtitle format when available, otherwise bounded-fetch/probe content type and signatures. Default safely to text/vtt or application/x-subrip only after validation.

findings.finding: Several PlayerEngine controls are implemented as no-ops or restricted on the Exo fallback route: subtitle delay, audio delay, audio output policy, full chapter support, DV/Atmos capture, and community trickplay capture.
findings.impact: The same Android UI exposes capabilities whose behavior changes materially when routing falls back from mpv to ExoPlayer.
findings.fix: Publish explicit engine capabilities and hide/disable unsupported controls. Port what Media3 supports; clearly label route-limited functions and add parity tests for capability/UI consistency.

findings.confidence: Confirmed by code comment; device impact unverified
findings.finding: Frame capture on the Surface-direct hardware-decoding path is knowingly unverified and may produce null or near-black images.
findings.impact: Scrub thumbnails and community trickplay contribution can fail on the main high-performance playback route.
findings.fix: Add device-matrix capture tests. Prefer a verified libmpv render API/readback path or a decoder-image route; gate contribution on luminance/variance validation rather than accepting black frames.

findings.finding: Tapping Download on an existing paused record calls resume but returns the stale pre-resume DownloadRecord value.
findings.impact: Callers can immediately render or reason from paused state even though the store changed to downloading/queued.
findings.fix: Return the post-mutation store record, or make resume return the updated record/state.

findings.finding: HLS asset downloads bypass the byte-download concurrency cap and queue.
findings.impact: The user's max-concurrent setting is not a true global limit; multiple HLS and byte tasks can exceed the intended network/storage pressure.
findings.fix: Use a shared scheduler with per-transport slots or clearly rename the setting to byte downloads only. Prefer a weighted global cap.

findings.finding: HLS detection is based on path extension or substring '.m3u8'.
findings.impact: Extensionless signed manifests are missed, while unrelated URLs containing the substring can be misclassified.
findings.fix: Use source metadata/content type when available; otherwise perform a bounded HEAD/range sniff and recognize #EXTM3U.

findings.finding: The V2 YouTube resolver/hardening path is compiled but disabled by default; client identities remain hard-coded with a TODO for remote configuration.
findings.impact: The newer resilience path is not protecting normal users, and hard-coded client identities are brittle when upstream behavior changes.
findings.fix: Finish staged remote configuration, telemetry and rollback; enable for a small cohort and remove the obsolete path after measured parity.

findings.finding: The new vortx-core engine is linked only into the native iOS target and runs only as a default-off shadow ranker. Swift remains authoritative and no result reaches the UI.
findings.impact: A substantial migration surface ships without product effect while maintaining two ranking implementations.
findings.fix: Define acceptance metrics, automate divergence reports, link equivalent targets, and remove one implementation once the new engine passes deterministic parity fixtures.

findings.finding: Two iOS product architectures remain: a WKWebView host and VortXiOSNative. The legacy host is retained pending native parity/cutover.
findings.impact: Release, entitlements, routing and feature work can diverge between two app shells.
findings.fix: Maintain a cutover checklist and telemetry, stop adding features to the legacy host, and remove it once the native target meets explicit parity gates.

findings.location: CoreBridge.swift, CredentialScope.swift, DebridResolver.swift, EngineStremioRepository.kt, PlayerScreen.kt, PlayerChrome.kt and others
findings.finding: Several core files are extremely large and mix transport, state, policy, persistence and UI concerns.
findings.impact: Review becomes non-local, tests require broad fixtures, and merge conflicts encourage accidental coupling.
findings.fix: Split around explicit state machines and interfaces: identity/session, transport, persistence, ranking, player terminal reducer, chrome capability model and platform adapters. Enforce size/complexity budgets gradually.

findings.finding: Profile selection supports PIN/Kids overlays, but per-profile own-account sign-in/switching is not wired. Switch outcomes are ignored and the current session carries over.
findings.impact: Profiles are not equivalent account boundaries on Android; selecting another profile may still use the previous Stremio account.
findings.fix: Make profile selection transactional: resolve account binding, require sign-in where needed, swap engine/session credentials, then publish active profile. Never ignore SwitchAccount/NeedsSignIn outcomes.

findings.finding: Several visible Home/Discover/detail toggles have no runtime consumer: curated rails, collections hub, detail financials, spoiler-safe/blur behavior, and poster-label visibility. One comment also incorrectly says mergeDiscoverSearch has no consumer even though VortXApp uses it.
findings.impact: Users can change settings that do nothing, while stale comments make future work error-prone.
findings.fix: Create a generated preference-to-consumer registry/test. Hide incomplete rows behind a development flag or wire each consumer before release. Remove stale annotations.

findings.finding: The Apple trailer metadata factory is not ported; Android's meta model lacks trailerStreams/trailerYouTubeID and callers must construct requests manually.
findings.impact: Trailer discovery and identity behavior can vary by caller and miss metadata available on Apple.
findings.fix: Move trailer request derivation into shared model/domain code and make all detail surfaces use it.

findings.finding: The Source Index/Singularity implementation is compiled but hard-disabled with isEnabled=false.
findings.impact: Remote config and supporting MOAT/identity code exist, but Android cannot contribute to or consume the community source pool.
findings.fix: Either remove/hide the dormant surface or complete consent, rollout, abuse controls, tests and remote kill-switch wiring before enabling it.

findings.finding: v2 sync document writes are disabled pending rollback ratchets and per-account version floors.
findings.impact: The hardened format is not the authoritative write path; migration remains incomplete.
findings.fix: Complete monotonic version-floor storage, rollback rejection, migration telemetry and cross-device compatibility tests, then enable staged v2 writes through remote config.

findings.finding: Android settings backup is primarily a profile-roster carrier; whole-domain settings export/import and the fuller Apple workflow are deliberately not ported.
findings.impact: Moving devices or restoring Android loses more configuration than Apple, despite shared key names.
findings.fix: Define a cross-platform backup schema with explicit domain allow-lists, secret exclusions, migrations and round-trip conformance fixtures.

findings.finding: Release staging labels the full flavor as phone and the play flavor as TV, although these flavors primarily describe engine/distribution and both packages include phone and TV activities.
findings.impact: Users and maintainers can select the wrong artifact and misunderstand feature differences.
findings.fix: Name artifacts by actual dimensions (full-mpv, play-media3, ABI, universal) and document device support separately.

findings.finding: Privileged release workflows lack equivalent secretless pull-request validation lanes.
findings.impact: The first complete exercise of packaging/signing-specific scripts can happen only after merge or during release.
findings.fix: Factor reusable build/test workflows and run unsigned/ad-hoc packaging on PRs. Keep signing/notarization as a thin protected final stage.

findings.finding: Backup envelope decoders do not strictly enforce the supported schema version and declared keyCount consistency.
findings.impact: Future or malformed payloads can be accepted under assumptions the importer does not actually support.
findings.fix: Require exact supported schema (or a defined migration path), verify keyCount, enforce duplicate-key and size limits, and reject unknown critical fields.

findings.finding: Cleartext traffic is enabled broadly for compatibility rather than narrowly scoped to known local/add-on cases.
findings.impact: More HTTP destinations can be contacted without transport security than the product likely needs.
findings.fix: Default deny cleartext. Permit loopback/private-network hosts through explicit runtime handling; require per-add-on opt-in and warnings for remote HTTP.

findings.finding: Download request headers are persisted as plaintext JSON in app-private storage.
findings.impact: Headers may contain bearer tokens, cookies, referers or proxy credentials. Backup exclusion reduces exposure but does not protect a compromised/debuggable device or diagnostic copy.
findings.fix: Persist only an allow-listed subset, redact secrets, or encrypt credential-bearing values with Android Keystore. Prefer re-resolving short-lived headers on resume.

findings.finding: An HMAC secret is provisioned into client apps with masking/obfuscation.
findings.impact: Any secret shipped to clients is recoverable and cannot be treated as a durable authorization boundary.
findings.fix: Use HMAC only for telemetry/abuse friction. Move privileged authorization to short-lived server-issued tokens, device attestation where appropriate, rate limiting, and server-side identity.

findings.confidence: Confirmed historical behavior documented in code
findings.finding: Older backup behavior could include token/data-key material. Current filtering self-heals synced documents but cannot revoke or repair backup files users already exported.
findings.impact: Previously exported files may remain sensitive even after upgrading.
findings.fix: Document affected versions, rotate exposed credentials where feasible, detect/import old envelopes cautiously, and notify users to delete/recreate legacy exports.

findings.location: DownloadStore load paths on both platforms
findings.finding: A corrupt or undecodable download index fails open to an empty record list; no backup repair or user-visible recovery is attempted.
findings.impact: A single partial/corrupt write can make every download disappear from the UI while files remain on disk.
findings.fix: Keep index.json and index.prev with checksums, validate before rotation, repair from the previous copy, scan the download directory for recoverable records, and surface a diagnostic event instead of silently returning empty.

findings.finding: The manual harness compiles only a small subset of the Apple test corpus and is not invoked by CI.
findings.impact: A large quantity of apparent test coverage is effectively documentation rather than an enforced quality gate.
findings.fix: Wire the harness into CI for its intended standalone contracts, and move the rest into real Xcode test targets.

findings.finding: A global transfer lock is held while an arbitrary file-I/O callback executes.
findings.impact: Slow disk operations serialize unrelated download control paths and raise ANR/deadlock risk if callbacks re-enter transfer state.
findings.fix: Use the lock only to claim a per-record mutation token, perform I/O outside it, then commit state with generation checks.

findings.finding: Download initialization launches an ad-hoc CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO) with no retained Job or structured owner.
findings.impact: The work cannot be cancelled, joined or observed and can outlive intended startup sequencing.
findings.fix: Use an application-owned SupervisorJob/scope or WorkManager for durable reconciliation, and expose completion/health.

findings.finding: Resume admission differs by load route: some paths seek for any positive start position while the normal path requires more than five seconds.
findings.impact: The same title can resume differently based on routing/format rather than user history.
findings.fix: Use one resume-admission policy shared by Exo, mpv, adaptive and offline paths, including floor and tail guard.

findings.finding: The file remains in the target, but AVPlayerEngine states that the bare HLSPlayerView path is no longer mounted; repository reference search finds no construction call.
findings.impact: Obsolete player code increases review surface and can be accidentally revived without current contracts.
findings.fix: Delete it after confirming no storyboard/reflection use, or move it under an explicit legacy target with a retirement issue.

findings.finding: The progressive resource-loader remux path is described as a rollback/legacy implementation, has no construction reference, lacks seeking and contains a Phase-2 TODO.
findings.impact: It preserves a second incomplete transport architecture alongside the HLS server.
findings.fix: Remove it if rollback is no longer needed; otherwise isolate it behind a compile flag and add a real owner/test.

findings.finding: Remote-config timeout dials for detail settle and debrid resolution are validated and documented but have no call-site consumers.
findings.impact: Operators may believe these controls can change production behavior; stale defaults can become a regression when eventually wired.
findings.fix: Either wire them with baked-equivalence tests or remove them from the schema until a consumer exists.

findings.finding: A generated Xcode build log is committed.
findings.impact: Repository noise, stale diagnostics and potential path/environment leakage.
findings.fix: Delete it and add the pattern to .gitignore.

findings.finding: The public core directory contains Cargo.lock but no public Cargo.toml/source tree.
findings.impact: The lockfile cannot build anything in the public checkout and suggests an incomplete/stale split.
findings.fix: Remove it, or publish the matching manifest/source/submodule contract and document how the private engine is supplied.

findings.location: ui/tv/TvApp.kt, TvSettingsScreen.kt, README and related comments
findings.finding: Several comments/readme sections describe older route or sign-in limitations that no longer match implemented screens.
findings.impact: Maintainers can duplicate work or preserve wrong assumptions during parity changes.
findings.fix: Make route/feature tables generated from capability declarations where possible; remove historical implementation notes from production source comments.

findings.finding: More Like This implements the TMDB leg but not Apple's add-on genre/catalog merge.
findings.impact: Recommendations are narrower and can diverge between platforms.
findings.fix: Port the merge/dedup/ranking policy into shared code and feed both platforms the same inputs.

findings.finding: Documentation says the update prompt is once per launch, but choosing Later persists the build key and suppresses that build across later launches.
findings.impact: Users may miss the same important update indefinitely.
findings.fix: Store a timestamp/backoff or session-only dismissal, and reserve permanent suppression for an explicit Skip This Version action.

findings.finding: Concurrent checks can access a plain mutable prompted-key set without synchronization.
findings.impact: Duplicate prompts or collection races are possible if startup/manual checks overlap.
findings.fix: Serialize checks with a Mutex/single-flight job and keep prompt state in StateFlow or a synchronized store.

findings.location: project files, workflows and public core tree
findings.finding: A fresh public checkout cannot reproduce every shipping target without private engine frameworks, generated artifacts and release credentials.
findings.impact: External contributors and automated auditors cannot independently compile the entire product.
findings.fix: Provide documented stubs or a public development mode, checksums/provenance for private binaries, and a manifest describing the exact missing inputs.

parity.capability: VortX account and encrypted cross-device sync
parity.apple: Implemented; v2 write migration still disabled

parity.android: Partial; selection carries current session and ignores switch outcome

parity.capability: Home, Discover, Search, Library and Live
Detail financials, spoiler-safe/blur and poster-label controls
Debrid, direct HTTP, torrent/streaming server and Usenet/TorBox paths

parity.apple: Implemented with native END_FILE reason handling
parity.android: Implemented in full flavor; END_FILE reason lost

parity.apple: Strong AVPlayer native-DV/remux path plus mpv

parity.capability: Audio/subtitle track selection and external subtitles
Subtitle delay, audio delay and output policy
parity.apple: Full on mpv; AVPlayer has route-specific no-ops
parity.android: Full on mpv; Exo has more no-ops

parity.apple: Implemented on AVPlayer and mpv routes
parity.android: Primarily mpv; direct-surface capture unverified, Exo limited

parity.capability: Skip intro/credits/community skip and autoplay flow

parity.android: Known gap: local Playable can use stale session identity

parity.apple: Implemented but has preflight/retry invariant bugs; HLS bypasses cap
parity.assessment: Near parity with Apple correctness gaps

parity.android: Implemented, but URL/digest trust needs hardening
